tamil-brahmi-1.era: c. 2nd c. BCE onward (orthographic system, not a strict period)

exceptions.text: No e/ē or o/ō contrast.
exceptions.source: I. Mahadevan, Early Tamil Epigraphy (2003; rev. 2014)

exceptions.text: Tamil-Brāhmī adds letters for the Tamil sounds ḻ, ḷ, ṟ and ṉ that Aśokan Brāhmī lacks (Unicode: BRAHMI LETTER OLD TAMIL LLLA/RRA/NNNA, U+11035–U+11037, and LLA U+11034).
exceptions.source: I. Mahadevan, Early Tamil Epigraphy (2003; rev. 2014); Unicode Standard, Brahmi block

exceptions.text: Tamil-Brāhmī writes Tamil and has no letters for Sanskrit aspirates or sibilants in this inventory; Prakrit loan words in the corpus may use a few Brāhmī letters (e.g. dha, sa) and are not part of the core set.
exceptions.source: I. Mahadevan, Early Tamil Epigraphy (2003; rev. 2014)

exceptions.text: Tamil-Brāhmī I: a bare consonant sign is the consonant without vowel; Ca is written with the same stroke as Cā (a/ā ambiguity).
exceptions.source: I. Mahadevan, Early Tamil Epigraphy (2003; rev. 2014)

exceptions.text: No e/ē or o/ō contrast.
exceptions.source: I. Mahadevan, Early Tamil Epigraphy (2003; rev. 2014)

exceptions.text: Tamil-Brāhmī II: the bare consonant sign carries inherent a (as in Aśokan Brāhmī), so a vowel-less consonant is not distinguished from Ca.
exceptions.source: I. Mahadevan, Early Tamil Epigraphy (2003; rev. 2014)

exceptions.source: I. Mahadevan, Early Tamil Epigraphy (2003; rev. 2014)

exceptions.text: Tamil-Brāhmī III: the pulli (dot) marks the vowel-less consonant; the bare sign is Ca.
exceptions.source: I. Mahadevan, Early Tamil Epigraphy (2003; rev. 2014)

vatteluttu.era: c. 6th–11th c. CE in the Tamil country

exceptions.text: Short and long e (e/ē) and o (o/ō) are written with the same sign; the distinction was introduced in the 18th century (attributed to C. J. Beschi). Editors supply the length in ISO transliteration, so the tutor accepts either value for these signs.
exceptions.source: standard history of Tamil script; DHARMA editions normalise length in transliteration

exceptions.text: The pulli (dot marking a vowel-less consonant) is usually not written in medieval stone inscriptions; a consonant sign may stand for C or Ca and must be read from context.
exceptions.source: general palaeographic observation; DHARMA editions transliterate the intended reading

exceptions.text: Vaṭṭeḻuttu has no Unicode encoding; Aksharamukha maps it to Tamil code points. The app ships SVG glyphs and shows the ISO-15919 value (contracts/restore-api.md).
exceptions.source: Aksharamukha ScriptMap/MainIndic/Vatteluttu.py; Unicode pipeline (not encoded)

exceptions.text: Sanskrit sounds (j, ś, ṣ, s, h) are not part of Vaṭṭeḻuttu; Sanskrit words are written in Grantha alongside it.
exceptions.source: DHARMA editions mark such passages with <hi rend='grantha'>

exceptions.text: Grantha writes Sanskrit: full Sanskrit inventory (aspirates, sibilants, r̥, l̥). e and o are long in Sanskrit; there is no short/long contrast to teach.
exceptions.source: Unicode Standard, Grantha block; Aksharamukha Grantha map

exceptions.text: Tamil-script inscriptions of this period write Sanskrit words with Grantha letters (j, ś, ṣ, s, h, kṣ); they are included and flagged grantha=true.
exceptions.source: DHARMA <hi rend='grantha'> markup (10,247 spans in the six collections)
